key_insight: Accurate tumor-growth predictions can still come from the wrong growth law, so model selection should check both fit quality and mathematical validity.
clinical_relevance: For precision oncology, this work suggests that automated tumor-model discovery must be interpreted cautiously because misleading equations could affect downstream forecasting and treatment planning.
method: Generate synthetic sparse/noisy tumor-growth data from Gompertz dynamics
Compare symbolic regression candidates using admissibility checks, coefficient refitting, and LLM-based ranking
Evaluate trajectory fit, forecasting, and recovered growth law separately
evidence_signal: In the abstract’s synthetic control, dense noiseless data recovered the true family, but sparse noisy data often produced alternative laws; nonlinear least squares usually improved law error, while PINN refitting often worsened it.
watch_item: LLM rankings and strong trajectory fits did not reliably indicate the correct governing equation, so implementation should not rely on prediction error alone.
paper_title: AI-Assisted Tumor-Growth Law Discovery from Sparse Data: Refitting and LLM-Based Ranking
